evidence_class: read-only original-image/static-contract review and independently recomputed analytical controls
result: No contradictory instruction, receiver identity, arithmetic, or custody error found in the bounded CRC1–CRC5 claims. This review does not close actual selected-source/project/engine rate reconciliation and does not authorize differing-rate placed timeline playback.
method: Parsed the immutable thin Mach-O header and LC_SEGMENT_64 mappings independently with Python struct; no peer address-mapping helper was imported.

Compared every listed native instruction word and complete REA memory readback in the author verification inventory directly with independently mapped original file bytes. Checked each listed REA instruction address lies within the exact retained readback and agrees with that source word.
Read original disassembly for the claimed caller, getter, setter, publication, constructor and branch chains; treated raw-slice decompiler types and missing indirect targets as advisory only.
Read original vtable pointer cells and followed table[-8] to RTTI typeinfo and typeinfo+8 to class-name strings. Checked three concrete class identities independently of author labels.

Recomputed all 24 rate controls using Fraction representations of the supplied binary64 values, explicit rounding after multiplication/division, binary32 pack/unpack for reader narrowing, and positive signed-integer truncation for the engine path. These are analytical controls, not execution of target instructions.

Rehashed all 436 local manifest entries and 63 external references. Independently confirmed the two duplicate records differ only in subject.local_path and checked the retained canonical import result reports 90 imported/90 total.

source_checks.semantic_scope: Focused CRC1–CRC5 call and state paths; whole listed inventory checked for byte custody, not a semantic review of every unrelated instruction or callback.

claims_reviewed.assessment: Supported within the inspected ordinary reader. Global VstDeck datum period is reciprocated in binary64, then narrowed to binary32 and widened; it is not a selected-source rate query or actual accessor rate setter.

Supported for the positive finite supplied-rate setter path. VstDeck uses the product of separate device-management rate and factor inputs; physical-device backend identity, startup order, replacement providers and callback mutations remain qualified.
The forwarded product/reciprocal receiver is the inspected TGTransport default, not SequencerEngine. Registry keys, constructor assignment and virtual slots agree.

Supported and numerically distinct from CRC1. FMUL is followed by signed32 FCVTZS, SCVTF back to binary64, current engine rate comparison, and conditional +0xa0 setter. This applies only to finite representable conversion inputs and the inspected provider path.

Supported for the stated valid channel/plane path. The ordinary/alternate decision tests state+0xa8 and channel+0x14c8 -> +0x258 byte+0x2ec. It is not a comparison of source and destination rates. The alternate receiver and mapping are not a complete reconstruction of rate mismatch handling.

analytical_control_check.interpretation: The same supplied rate/factor pair can produce distinct reader and engine stored numeric values. This disproves substituting the engine integer for the reader multiplier in a model; it is not an observed target playback discrepancy.

remaining_boundaries: Builder root+0x128 provider, selected source stream rate, VstDeck period, SequencerEngine rate and physical device rate are not interchangeable identities.
Upstream grouped stream normalization selects the first collected reference stream; its collection ordering and equality to requested event, project, engine or device rate remain unproved.
Direct/curve/inversion selected streams can retain source rate. No complete path that reconciles an arbitrary differing source/project rate is established by these findings.
Registry replacements, callbacks, actual host state and alternate interpolation lifecycle may alter the examined conditions. The report is not a universal rate-setting or scheduler contract.
All controls are static or analytical. No Cubase execution, audio driver activation, live native playback, DAC capture, target export or target sample comparison was performed.
review_execution_note: The first ephemeral byte-check attempt stopped on a reviewer parser assumption that REA assembly rows were objects; the retained provider rows are strings. The corrected parser verified all listed counts. No input, study, or application file was changed by that attempt.
